gen-flavors-gf-savate: Soft, cheeky, stubby-pencil letters from Flavors sit up top. Savate runs on sturdy hairlines and open curves, so paragraphs of it keep moving without tiring the eye for long.
gen-fraunces-archivo: Lightly engraved brass lettering, dignified and a little bookish. Fraunces is best at modest contrast and generously opened curves, while Archivo is best at lowercase height that commands the line.
gen-fraunces-fs-spline-sans: Spline Sans reads flat and friendly, with unmodulated strokes and generous gaps where curves meet the stems. Long paragraphs would glide along smoothly, with Fraunces holding the dignified top.
gen-fraunces-space-grotesk: Dignified Fraunces leads with generous curve openings and gently varied line weight. And Space Grotesk, drawn at the width of one stylus, carries a long paragraph without a stumble.
gen-fredoka-gf-lisu-bosa: Soft, friendly, one-width letters with a bounce. Fredoka keeps its single pen line and open e, while Lisu Bosa adds classic, tall, sturdy lowercase with counters spilling outward.
gen-fs-be-vietnam-pro-fs-karma: Crisp sans up top, a settled serif below. Be Vietnam Pro is best at constant stroke width and daylight in its curves, while Karma is best at quiet, classic modulation.
gen-fs-be-vietnam-pro-roboto-slab: Marker-drawn curves meet a structured slab. Be Vietnam Pro keeps its tall midsection and constant strokes, while Roboto Slab packs a dominant middle zone with open throats, so they feel precise together.
gen-fs-bespoke-stencil-fs-fira-sans: Bespoke Stencil stamps in with industrial command, then Fira Sans replies in tubelike lines of constant weight. The standout is Fira Sans's larger-than-usual x-height, which keeps every line legible.
gen-fs-bevellier-gf-graduate: Graduate reads dignified and bookish, with generous white between letters and capitals nearly level with the lowercase. And Bevellier crowns it with stencil-cut, single-weight lettering that sits graceful and tight.
gen-fs-bevellier-noto-serif: Bevellier brings a stencil-cut, single-weight look with a high, wide lowercase, while Noto Serif adds a modest pencil-line taper. Better for a few paragraphs than for a whole chapter.
